Chapter 1: How People Once Heard Gods Instead of Themselves
Picture this for a moment: you’re living in a world where your own inner voice doesn’t feel like yours at all.
Instead, any nudge or urge comes through as a presence—sometimes gentle, sometimes booming—telling you what to do, almost like someone else is inside your head, calling the shots.
For us today, our minds are these private sanctuaries, right? We plan, we ponder, we replay conversations in our heads. But go back thousands of years, and the mind wasn’t a quiet, personal retreat—it was more like a crowded stage, where powerful voices made their entrance and exit, always sounding unmistakably real and, above all, external.
Life back then was unpredictable.
Crops sometimes just failed. Storms rolled in out of nowhere. Even the rules that held society together were still taking shape.
And in all that uncertainty, people talked about hearing voices—clear, commanding, impossible to ignore.
But here’s the thing: these voices weren’t brushed off as wild imagination or signs of illness. No, they were accepted as the voice of the gods, ancestors, or spirits—guiding every step, from the everyday to the extraordinary.
Picture a farmer, standing in his field, unsure if it’s the right time to plant. Suddenly, a voice—familiar but somehow not his own—tells him, “Start now.”
And he listens. Not because he’s frightened or confused, but because that’s just how decisions were made. That voice felt as real as the sun on his face, and it carried all the authority of the divine.
And this wasn’t just a rare thing. Whole societies were shaped by it.
If you read the ancient stories—the Iliad, old Sumerian tablets—you’ll notice heroes and kings don’t just wonder what to do. They get direct messages from gods. Advice, warnings, commands—it’s all delivered with such matter-of-fact clarity, you get the sense this was just everyday life.
Now, most of us today would call that a hallucination.
But back then? These voices were just part of how the world worked. They gave people structure and comfort in a world that could feel pretty chaotic.
The line between your own thoughts and an outside command wasn’t nearly as sharp as it is for us now.
Of course, as time went on—societies grew, writing spread, and things began to change.
But for a long chapter of human history, people didn’t just listen to their own minds. They listened for the voice of the gods.
